---
title: "Installation"
description: "Build and install Wraptool from source with Go or the repository Guix manifest."
---

## Current distribution status

Wraptool is currently installed from source. The repository does not yet publish
versioned binary archives or packages, so do not rely on a download URL or a
package-manager name.

## Build with Go

Clone the repository, then build the main package with Go 1.26.0 or newer (the
version declared by `go.mod`):

```bash
git clone https://forge.snamellit.com/pti/wraptool.git
cd wraptool
go build -o wraptool .
./wraptool version
```

Move the resulting binary to a directory on your `PATH` using the installation
conventions for your system. Using `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` makes a version mismatch
fail rather than downloading a toolchain implicitly.

```bash
GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build -o wraptool .
```

## Build with Guix

The repository's flat `manifest.scm` supplies Go, Git, Quarto, Node, the linter,
and shell utilities used by development and containers:

```bash
guix shell -m manifest.scm -- go build -o wraptool .
guix shell -m manifest.scm -- ./wraptool version
```

Guix package versions depend on the caller's channel state; the repository does
not currently include a `channels.scm` lock. Review changes to `manifest.scm`
before evaluating it because Guix manifests are executable Scheme.

## Verify the checkout

```bash
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go build -o wraptool .
./wraptool --help
```

The full contributor checks, including formatting and `golangci-lint`, are in
[Contributing](contributing.qmd).

## Runtime dependencies

Wraptool itself is a Go binary. Individual features need additional host tools:

| Feature | Host dependency |
|---|---|
| Wrapped CLI | The configured absolute binary and any helpers it launches |
| `up --runtime=guix` | `guix`, plus `manifest.scm` in the worktree |
| `up --runtime=devcontainer` | `devcontainer` and its container runtime |
| Harness installation | Guix for automated pool installers; otherwise use the Dev Container feature |

Proceed to [Getting started](getting-started.qmd) to create a policy and launch
the server.
